question: A febrile patient's first peripheral blood smear is reported as 'no malaria parasites seen.' Clinical suspicion remains high. What is the MOST appropriate next step?

answers.text: Repeat thick and thin blood smears at 12-hour intervals

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Peripheral blood smear (thick + thin films, Giemsa-stained) is the gold standard for malaria diagnosis. Parasitaemia can be low or cyclical, so a single negative smear does not exclude malaria. Repeating at 12-hour intervals (up to 3 sets over 48 hours) is standard when clinical suspicion is high.

answers.text: Conclude that malaria is excluded and investigate other causes of fever

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A single negative smear does not rule out malaria — parasitaemia may be too low for detection, especially in early infection or partially treated cases. Standard practice is to repeat smears at 12-hour intervals before concluding malaria is absent.

answers.text: Order a Widal test to check for enteric fever instead

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While enteric fever is in the differential, a single negative smear does not exclude malaria. Widal testing may be added in parallel, but it should not replace repeat smear testing when malaria is clinically suspected.

Incorrect. While empirical treatment may be justified in severe cases in endemic areas, the standard approach is to repeat smears at 12-hour intervals to confirm the diagnosis and identify the species — species identification determines the treatment regimen.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: peripheral blood smear (thick + thin, Giemsa-stained) is the gold standard. A single negative smear does not exclude malaria — repeat at 12-hour intervals when clinical suspicion is high. RDTs can provide interim results while awaiting repeat smears.

Exactly right. The peripheral blood smear is the gold standard, but low parasitaemia means one negative smear is insufficient. Repeat at 12-hour intervals. RDTs can supplement but not replace smear examination.
